headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 15 of the 19 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
A chilly overnight period tonight will be followed by quiet and dry weather well into mid week.
Dry and seasonable conditions continue through next weekend.

ALY.excerpt: ) Despite a developing Nor'Easter, dry weather is expected across eastern New York and western New England through much of the upcoming week.

GYX.excerpt: High pressure will be in control most of the upcoming week, bringing fair weather and near normal daytime temperatures.

PHI.excerpt:
Frost concerns for portions of the area later tonight into early Monday morning.
A nor'easter developing off the coast of the southern Mid- Atlantic is expected to bring coastal impacts and create hazardous marine conditions through at least the middle of this week.
A prolonged period of onshore flow will lead to multiple elevated high tide cycles this week resulting in rounds of coastal flooding.

CTP.excerpt:
) Frost/freeze tonight for areas where the growing season remains active.
) Extended stretch of dry and seasonable weather this week.

RLX.excerpt:
) Strong radiational cooling will yield more chances for frost and freeze conditions tonight and once again Monday night. A Frost Advisory is in place for locations remaining in the active growing season late tonight into Monday morning. Temperatures are anticipated to slowly moderate through the course of the week.
) A stretch of dry weather, courtesy of high pressure, will triumph through the work week into next weekend.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Dry, with cold nights.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:28}} to {{t:55}}, mostly dry.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 18).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Sunday 7:35 PM: "A chilly overnight period tonight will be followed by quiet and dry weather well into mid week."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and slightly drier than normal.
